message.content: Trade gave pharaohs more power. They used it, because their goods, their wealth, and their influence grew. We can see this: when merchants brought grain, gold, and ships, the state controlled them, taxed them, and rewarded their loyalty. Pharaohs could then build temples, armies, and tombs; they also relied on their officials, but they kept their own authority. If rivals challenged them, the pharaoh’s people, his guards, and their alliances could respond. I think you can see how we should treat them: he, she, and it all show why their success mattered, and my view is that their rulers, their armies, and their neighbors benefited from it.
